title: session middleware and stream cancellation shim across Python/TS/Go SDKs
author: Aisha Mendez
description: Motivation: multiple teams reported subtle inconsistencies between SDKs around token refresh semantics and streaming cancellation ergonomics which make cross-language client behavior fragile under transient auth failures and client-side aborts. This PR introduces a lightweight SessionMiddleware abstraction and a StreamCancelToken shim implemented in Python, TypeScript, and Go to unify retry/backoff behavior, document lifetime of long-lived streams, and provide a single hook for token rotation and diagnostics. Changes include a consolidated RetryPolicy config (retry.window -> retry.window_ms and a deprecation shim), SessionMiddleware that centralizes credential refresh + per-session metadata (client_id, region, last_healthy_at), an opt-in StreamCancelToken that allows application-level cancellation of active streaming iterators without tearing down underlying network connections, and cross-sdk test harnesses that verify parity for 1) auth-refresh-before-request, 2) in-flight stream reauth (graceful reconnect), and 3) abort-without-leak semantics. This is a cross-repo SDK change touching SDK clients in redwood-sdk-python, redwood-sdk-typescript, and redwood-sdk-go; it also adds a small server-side compatibility shim in the redwood monorepo to emit structured stream preamble events used by the cancel token. Backwards compatibility: default behavior preserved; migration path documented; small config rename documented with deprecation logs for one release. Linear tickets: ENG-4219 and ENG-4235. See commits_summary and changed_files for details.
release_notes: Cross-SDK: add SessionMiddleware (centralized credential refresh), StreamCancelToken (graceful client cancel), unify RetryPolicy config keys. No breaking runtime changes; config rename deprecated for one release. Bumped SDK versions: python 0.28.0, typescript 1.14.0, go v0.10.0.
commits_summary: 5 commits: initial middleware interfaces and types, python implementation and unit tests, typescript implementation and documentation, go implementation and integration tests, server-side stream preamble feature flag and compatibility tests.
review_comments: Evan Park: Can the SessionMiddleware be composed so existing users can opt-in without API churn? Author: yes, middleware is opt-in and we added a helper factory in each SDK to wrap the existing Client with minimal code change.

Diego Ruiz: The rename retry.window -> retry.window_ms will surprise some infra configs; we should emit a clear deprecation warning and a mapping layer. Author: added a compatibility shim that accepts both keys and logs a WARN once per process.
Priya Nair: Tests flaked in the GH matrix on go streaming cancellation. Author: added deterministic timeouts and a backoff stub to the go harness; reran CI and all jobs are green.
QA (manual): Verified canary on staging with a low-traffic Dedicated pool, confirmed no leaked goroutines or hung sockets after repeated cancels.
testing: unit: python pytest suite covers credential rotation and cancel token semantics
integration: cross-language streaming interop matrix in GH Actions (py/ts/go)
canary: staged Dedicated pool run for 48 hours to validate connection reuse and cancel frequency
notes_migration: Migration notes: 1) default behavior unchanged; to opt into SessionMiddleware call Client.with_session_middleware(SessionConfig(...)) or set SDK_SESSION_MIDDLEWARE=enabled. 2) rename retry.window -> retry.window_ms supported for one release; update config files to the _ms variant to avoid deprecation warnings. 3) StreamCancelToken is opt-in; see examples/streaming for usage patterns and cleanup recommendations.
